To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the genome organization shows multi-scale long-range correlations, that these correlations are fine-structured, and that these correlations are evolutionarily controlled and related closely to the genome three-dimensional organization.

the genome sequences of all completely sequenced organisms studied show fine-structured multi-scalarity of correlations on the scale from a few base pairs to a few million base pairs, and that the origin of these correlations can be attributed to a block organization of the genome and to nucleosomal binding, and that these correlations are evolutionarily conserved.

the sequential organization of genomes can be described by a multi-scaling behaviour of local correlation coefficients, that the multi-scaling is species-specific, that a fine-structure can be explained by codon usage, that a large-scale correlation maximum can be related to nucleosomal DNA binding, and that computer-generated random sequences assuming block organization of genomes and the codon usage explain these findings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sequential organization of genomes and its relation to the three-dimensional genome organization.
the question of whether there are any long-range correlations between distant regions within a chromosome and, if so, how these can be classified.
the sequential organization of genomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multi-scaling behaviour of the correlation coefficients is a feature of genomes and that it is related to the three-dimensional genome organization.
the genome is a complex system with many levels of organization, and that these levels of organization are connected to each other, and to the genome's function.
genomes have a multi-scaling long range correlation structure that is fine-structured and species-specific.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new, complex, multi-scaling, fine-structured sequential organization of genomes.
the three-dimensional genome organization is a result of the sequential genome organization, which is evolutionarily tightly controlled.
the three-dimensional organization is reflected in the sequential organization of genomes.
